fatal_errors: No specific Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived FCC single-crystal material or initial state is identified.
The proposed monotonic thermal softening misses cryogenic strengthening, low-temperature inertial dulling, and elevated-temperature Portevin-Le Chatelier strengthening.
The outcome is framed as greater plastic strain rather than the target quantities of CRSS, strain-rate sensitivity, serrated flow, and composition-dependent strengthening.
The proposed tensile test does not reconstruct the [1̄23]-oriented single-crystal compression experiment or distinguish the relevant mechanisms.
explanation: The hypothesis only captures the generic fact that temperature affects dislocation motion in metals. It does not identify the relevant equiatomic FCC medium/high-entropy alloys, their single-crystal condition, the 9–1373 K compression protocol, or the composition dependence. Its simple claim that heating lowers yield strength conflicts with the observed high-temperature serrated-flow and CRSS increase caused by dynamic Mn/Fe solute pinning, while entirely omitting MSAD-controlled solid-solution strength and phonon-drag-controlled inertial behavior below roughly 60–77 K. The suggested experiment could measure generic thermal deformation but cannot discriminate Cottrell versus Suzuki pinning, inertial dulling, or lattice-distortion scaling.
